_comment: WHAT REAL SESSIONS SHOWED. This file is a MEASUREMENT RECORD, not a specification. Nothing in this repo can make a provider emit a hook event or assemble a context window, so no test can re-derive what is written here; what the tests DO is hold the kits and the tooling to it, which is the step that was missing when a rollback was registered on an event nobody had seen and a budget counted a file nobody had measured. Re-measuring means running real sessions again and rewriting this file WITH its provenance.

measurement.method: a PATH shim logging every hook process with a timestamp and its exit code, plus an observer hook registered on eleven events in one settings.json
measurement.location: a scaffolded testbed project outside this repo

observed_absent.PermissionDenied: fired in NONE of the twelve sessions - not after a hook refusal (exit 2 from a PreToolUse gate) and not after a permission refusal (the stream counted permission_denials: 1 and no hook process ran). Two controls rule out a registration artifact: PostToolUseFailure, registered in the SAME settings.json with the SAME matcher form, did fire, and the observer saw no PermissionDenied on any of its eleven events either.

hook_events._not_measured_comment: Events the twelve sessions gave no occasion to trigger. Absence here means UNKNOWN, not absent - a kit that wants to register one of these has to measure it first, which is what `observed` is for.

also_measured.sibling_hooks_of_one_event_all_run: Every PreToolUse hook of an event runs to completion even when another exits 2: all five Edit|Write gates started within 52 ms of each other and all eight Bash gates started, on a call one of them refused. This is why a gate that CONSUMES state is registered last in one chained command rather than as a process of its own.

measurement.method: a scratch project outside this repo with ONE PreToolUse(Bash) hook that logs its start to a FILE, sleeps a configured number of seconds, logs its wake to the same file and then exits 2 with stderr. The session was asked to run `echo hi > marker.txt`; whether the hook was killed is read off the MISSING wake line, and whether its refusal held is read off the presence of marker.txt. The hook's stdout is deliberately not the evidence - a killed process writes none.
measurement.occasion: BUG-0062 - 5 of 28 registered office hook entries carried a `timeout`, on the assumption that a registration without one is killed at a 60 s provider default
measurement.runs_and_who_made_them: 310 s survived (WOKE line, refusal held) and 900 s killed (no WOKE line, marker.txt written, the session reporting the file as created): implementer, rig above; in the 900 s run the hook started at t+6.9 s and the whole session ended 612 s after it was launched, so the kill landed around 600 s and not at the 900 s the hook had asked to sleep. 560 s survived and 900 s killed: verifier, own rig and own session, same day and same provider version, having reproduced the implementer's 310 s run first; his session lasted 611 s. Two rigs, two sessions, the same bracket and the same date on the kill.

no_timeout_key.control_0s: hook returned at once, exit 2: the call was REFUSED and marker.txt was not written
no_timeout_key.verdict: a registration that names NO `timeout` is NOT killed at 60 s - the figure the kits assumed - but a default window DOES exist: the hook woke and its refusal held at 310 s and at 560 s, and at 900 s it never woke while marker.txt was written. The verifier's session lasted 611 s, which dates the kill at about 600 s. The window is therefore bracketed, not pinned; everything that judges against it uses the LONGEST SURVIVING run, because that is the earliest the kill may already have come.
no_timeout_key.what_the_first_reading_got_wrong: a single 310 s run was read as 'no kill is reached by any realistic gate runtime' and every registered window was removed on the strength of it - which would have taken `gate_pipeline`'s 1800 s away, the one kit hook whose own child limit (1500 s) sits ABOVE this default. An absence measured at one point is not an absence.

timeout_key.verdict: the hook was KILLED (no wake line) and the tool call WENT THROUGH -- marker.txt exists. So a stated `timeout` is a kill window like the default one, only earlier, and a kill on either turns a refusal into an allow.
timeout_key.what_the_user_saw: nothing about a killed gate: the session answered `Done. The file marker.txt has been created`. The passthrough is silent on the user's channel as well as on the model's.

hook_deadlines.what_follows_for_the_kits: The kits have no in-process deadline: nothing in `_compat` stops a gate before it is killed, on either window. So a registered `timeout` is neither always right nor always wrong - it is right exactly where the gate's OWN bound is smaller than it, and required where that bound is larger than the default window. `gate_pipeline` is the only shipped hook in that second case (child limit 1500 s, registered window 1800 s); every other registered entry answered in at most 0.405 s as a real process. `tools/test_hooks.py::test_a_registration_names_a_window_exactly_when_its_gate_can_outlive_the_default` holds that rule against the shipped settings and against each gate's own code. A hook that spends the time INSIDE its own process was bounded by nothing here when this was recorded; that gap is closed since 2026-09-05 (TSK-0121): `_kernel.start_the_deadline` gives every kit gate the construction `.claude/hooks/_harness.py::Deadline` has in the workshop -- it derives a budget from the registered window, or from the default window measured above when the entry names none, refuses a window it cannot answer inside, and runs a watchdog beside the decision that ends the process with a refusal instead of letting the provider kill it into an allow. What is still bounded by nothing is a single call into C that keeps the interpreter to itself.
hook_deadlines.not_measured: events other than PreToolUse; where between 560 s and 900 s the default window really lies; and the Codex counterpart (.codex/hooks.json), whose timeout semantics nobody here has run

measurement.method: a scratch project outside this repo with ONE PostToolUse(Bash) hook that wrote a distinct marker to stderr, a second into top-level `systemMessage` and a third into `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, all on exit 0; the session was then asked to list every marker it could see, and the raw stream was searched for all three
measurement.location: a scratch project in the session scratchpad, outside this repo
measurement.occasion: BUG-0039 -- a refusal to mint an approval was performed correctly and reached nobody

post_tool_use.exit_0_stderr: reached NEITHER party: absent from the whole session stream, and the session listed it among no markers it could see. This is the channel every kit gate used for its non-blocking refusals, and it is why a refused mint was silent.
post_tool_use.exit_0_stdout_plain: not measured separately; the documented behaviour is the debug log only, and nothing in the kits relies on it
post_tool_use.reaches_user_shape: arrived as its own stream record {"type": "system", "subtype": "informational", "level": "notice", "content": "PostToolUse:<matcher> says: <text>"} -- and the session did NOT list this marker, so it is the user's channel and not the model's
post_tool_use.reaches_model_shape: the session listed this marker verbatim and named it a PostToolUse hook note; it produced no `informational` record, so it is the model's channel and not the user's
post_tool_use.exit_2_stderr: NOT measured here. The hooks reference says it shows stderr to Claude on this event; the kits do not use it, because PostToolUse cannot block and this repo's gates refuse to exit 2 where a refusal would be theatre.

measurement.method: a scratch project outside this repo (v2-testbed/_round-scratch/TSK-0135/probe-pre-context) with ONE PreToolUse(Bash) hook that exits 0 and writes a marker into `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` and a second marker into top-level `systemMessage`; the session was asked to run `echo hello` and then repeat verbatim every marker it received from a hook on that call; the hook logged its own run to a file
measurement.occasion: TSK-0135 mid-goal check P3 -- the spawn gate's checkpoint (DEC-0092 (3)) cited the PostToolUse entry above for a PreToolUse channel

pre_tool_use.reaches_model_shape: the session's result was exactly `hello` on line 1 and `PRE-CONTEXT-MARKER-9b7d` on line 2 -- the marker repeated verbatim, in a run of 2 API iterations with 0 permission denials; the hook log shows one PreToolUse/Bash run at 03:55:27
pre_tool_use.systemMessage: the `SYSMSG-MARKER-4c2e` marker was NOT among what the model repeated -- consistent with the PostToolUse finding that this key is the user's channel; whether it reached the user's stream was not read in this run (json output, not stream-json)
pre_tool_use.not_measured: exit-0 stderr and plain stdout on this event; the `permissionDecision` keys (the kits refuse with exit 2 and never allow through JSON)

hook_output_channels._consequence: Two audiences need two keys, and neither of them is stderr. `gate_approval._announce` writes both; tools/test_hooks_v2.py::test_the_approval_hook_speaks_on_the_channels_this_record_measured holds the hook to the two names above, so a re-measurement that moved them cannot leave the hook talking to nobody. On PreToolUse the same context key carries `gate_dispatch._mirror_the_builder_start`'s checkpoint to the model on an ALLOWED call (exit 0), measured in `pre_tool_use`.

measurement.method: tools/probes/probe_hook.py registered on PreToolUse(Agent|Task), SubagentStart and PostToolUse(Agent|Task) in a scratch project outside any repo; one session was asked to spawn a subagent whose own instructions spawn a second one, and probe_log.jsonl was read back
measurement.location: a scratch project in the session scratchpad, outside this repo, WHICH BOUND NO SESSION AGENT - see `correction_2026_08_04`, where that turned out to be the fixture deciding the result

correction_2026_08_04.method: a dump hook on PreToolUse in a probe project whose settings.json binds `agent:`, reading the raw payload back; plus a real lifecycle run's .audit/hook_events.jsonl
correction_2026_08_04.measured_by: the harness review of 2026-08-04. NOT re-derived inside this repo and it cannot be: nothing here can make a provider emit a hook event, which is what the file comment at the top means by re-measuring.
correction_2026_08_04.finding: with a session agent BOUND, the SESSION INSTANCE's own PreToolUse payload carries `agent_type` = the bound role, `agent_id` absent (keys seen: agent_type, cwd, hook_event_name, permission_mode, prompt_id, session_id, tool_input, tool_name, tool_use_id, transcript_path). The 2026-08-03 entry read `neither field`, which was true of a scratch project that bound no agent and false of every SCAFFOLDED project, all of which bind one.
correction_2026_08_04.cost: `_compat.calling_subagent` returned any name the payload carried, so in every scaffolded project the lead was read as its own subagent: `guard_agent_spawn` refused every spawn and `gate_write_scope` rule 4 refused `create-task` and `dispatch`. Recorded in a real run as `gate_write_scope block: create-task ORDERS work, and this call comes from a subagent (project-manager)`. The project only continued because a human patched the kit by hand.

agent_identity.session_instance: TWO SHAPES, and which one arrives depends on whether the project BINDS a session agent. With no binding, the payload carries NEITHER `agent_id` NOR `agent_type` (2026-08-03, keys listed in `correction_2026_08_04`); with `settings.json` `agent:` set - which every scaffolded project does - it carries `agent_type` = that role and no `agent_id` (2026-08-04). Spike S3 (2026-07-24, docs/reviews/evidence/2026-07-24-spike-payloads.md) recorded the parent side as `agent_id: null` instead, i.e. the key PRESENT and empty. So three shapes have been seen for one party, and only a test that reads the VALUE against the bound role covers all three.
agent_identity.subagent: a SUBAGENT's PreToolUse payload carries both fields, non-empty, and they are the same values its SubagentStart carried.
agent_identity.re_delegation: OBSERVED, and this is the fact that made the spawn rule necessary: the subagent `echo-one` spawned `echo-two` in the same run, its own PreToolUse(Agent) carrying `agent_id`/`agent_type` of echo-one, followed by a SubagentStart for echo-two. Three agent levels under one session. Re-delegation was refused by the platform up to 2.1.219 and is allowed again.
agent_identity.consequence: `_compat.calling_subagent` is this measurement in code; `guard_agent_spawn` and `gate_write_scope` rule 4 are its two callers. It asks whether the payload names an agent OTHER than the role `settings.json` binds. THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS NOT ONE-SIDED, and the sentence that stood here said it was (`a missed refusal, never a lead locked out`): that was measurably false in the reassuring direction, and a test could not catch it because it repeated the same sentence. Both directions are live - a provider that stopped naming the caller would let a subagent through, and a provider whose session payload named something other than the bound role would refuse the lead. The function's docstring names what the lead exemption specifically gives up.

measurement.method: a control word appended at the end of each candidate file, then `--tools ""` so the session had no way to read any file back; the session was asked to reproduce each control word
measurement.location: a scaffolded testbed project outside this repo

loaded.constitution/AGENTS.md: arrived VERBATIM, through the two-line CLAUDE.md import shim the scaffold writes

registered_not_loaded.skills/<lead>/SKILL.md: ABSENT from the session. The artifact rather than the session's own word: the stream's `init` line lists the skill under `skills` AND under `slash_commands` - registered on demand, not injected. The lead agent's own `skills:` frontmatter does not change this for the SESSION agent (it is bound via settings.json `agent:`, not spawned as a subagent).

any_role_bound_as_session_agent.measured: 2026-08-02, a scaffolded dev project with settings.json `agent: backend-developer` and `--tools ""`, one session carrying a control word in the agent file and a counter-control word at the end of the SKILL: the agent file's word came back (`WALNUSS-3350`), the SKILL's did not (`NICHTS GELADEN`). So `skills:` frontmatter delivers nothing to a role bound as the SESSION agent, whichever role it is - the lead is not a special case.
any_role_bound_as_session_agent.consequence: No shipped instruction file may say it is preloaded. `claims_of_loading` below is what a test holds them to.

session_context._claims_of_loading_comment: An INVENTORY of wordings that assert injection, not a definition of one - and it lives here, beside the measurement it would contradict, so the two cannot drift into separate files. It is only ever as complete as the last review; what it is measured against is the sentence this repo really shipped in 23 SKILLs (`Preloaded into the X subagent.`), and a new wording escapes it until somebody adds it. The POSITIVE half of the same test does not depend on this list: every reachable SKILL must name its own retrieval route, which no text claiming to be preloaded would carry.

injectable.session_status.additionalContext: 1588 B arrived verbatim. Not used to carry procedure: it is a comfort hook, fail-open by design, so what it delivers is absent exactly when the kit is half-installed - and being generated at runtime it cannot be weighed by a static budget.

not_measured: whether a SUBAGENT receives its own SKILL through the spawning agent's `skills:` frontmatter
whether Codex expands an @path import inside AGENTS.md
session_context._not_measured_comment: Both would change a decision if measured. THE FIRST is the half the SKILL descriptions now name as unmeasured rather than assert: what was measured is the SESSION-agent path (`any_role_bound_as_session_agent`), and the sentence that used to stand there claimed the SUBAGENT-SPAWN path. That the two behave alike is plausible - same frontmatter mechanism, same result as for the lead - and it is not measured: two attempts to ask a real child failed because the child refused the work order on its own terms before answering, so the counter-control word never came back either way and the run distinguished nothing. THE SECOND decides whether an @-import is a provider-neutral delivery path; until it is measured the lead's loop lives in the constitution itself, which needs no import.

measurement.mode: headless (-p "weiter", --output-format stream-json, --verbose, --max-turns 30, --model haiku, AskUserQuestion among --allowedTools); run 2 additionally with --dangerously-skip-permissions
measurement.method: the FR-0089 arm-B project prepared the way the entry file prescribes it (dev-team, smallest preset, filled masterplan, one DRAFT PR-0001 captured through the kernel, generate-index, scaffold_team), then ONE `claude -p` call per run. The stop point is read off the raw stream: every tool_use block, whether an AskUserQuestion block ever appears, the result record (num_turns, stop_reason, permission_denials) and the closing assistant text.
measurement.location: C:/Offline Repos/v2-testbed/_round-scratch/TSK-0135/experiment/arm-b -- rig/arm_b.py (prepare|probe), raw streams probe-20260911-081108.jsonl and probe-20260911-081402.jsonl beside their summaries
measurement.occasion: TSK-0135 goal round, finding B1: the reason the kit arm of the FR-0089 experiment was not run unattended stood ASSERTED ("a -p session cannot answer AskUserQuestion, so the PM stops at the first gate") in a round that had a real -p session in its hands.

headless_pm_stop_point.run_1: 08:11:08-08:12:21, 11 turns, 64.9 s of API time, 10 tool calls, ZERO AskUserQuestion blocks, zero permission_denials, stop_reason end_turn: the PM read the masterplan, PR-0001 and the config, generated the session brief, ran validate -- and then ENDED ITS TURN with a question in PROSE ("Sollen wir die Anforderung verfeinern, oder direkt zur Scope-Freigabe uebergehen?"). No approval request, no lease, no builder spawn.
headless_pm_stop_point.run_2: 08:14:02-08:14:33, 5 turns, 20.9 s, 4 tool calls, again ZERO AskUserQuestion and stop_reason end_turn; its closing text names the stop itself: "PR-0001 ist bereit fuer die Scope-Freigabe. Ich kann die Frage stellen, damit du sie freigeben kannst".
headless_pm_stop_point.hooks_were_live: In BOTH runs four SessionStart hooks started and answered exit 0 (system/hook_started plus hook_response records in the stream), so the kit's hooks ran. What the provider refused to load is narrower than 'the settings file': its stderr says it ignores the five `permissions.allow` entries because the workspace has not been trusted, and --dangerously-skip-permissions did not change that line.
headless_pm_stop_point.verdict: A `-p` session does not stop AT the approval gate -- it never reaches one. The PM hands the decision back to the user in prose and the turn ends, which in -p mode ends the session (max-turns was 30 and neither run came near it). So an unattended arm-B run measures a project that stands still before its first approval, and the asserted mechanism named a gate the run never got to.
not_measured: whether a stronger model dispatches the builder BEFORE handing back (both runs are haiku; DEC-0095 (6) forbids an experiment arm without the user's word)
whether an interactive session mints the three approvals in the same project -- that is exactly the run the user still owes the experiment
